title: Every four-dimensional Kakeya set has full Hausdorff dimension
main_claim: Any set K in R^4 that contains a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension 4. K does not need to be measurable or compact. The proof works by contradiction: a counterexample is turned into a weighted line problem with a positive "horizon" (minimum time cost), and a positive horizon is then excluded through critical-path extremality in three narrowness regimes (ell = 0, 0 < ell < infinity, ell = infinity).

issues.description: Not a defect found, but a dependency. Both the initial horizon bound (H <= L) and the inequality g(0,0) <= 0 in the reduction rest entirely on the weighted full-time plank estimate. The paper does not prove it; it cites it as Lemma 2.3 of the companion OpenAI 3D Kakeya maximal preprint, with the hypotheses 'precisely' matching. The 4D result is therefore conditional on that companion paper, which I did not audit. The family board had no sibling report on it.
issues.evidence: "This is the indexed weighted formulation of [ThreeDimensional, Lemma~2.3]... The cited statement permits arbitrary positive weights and repeated indices, and has precisely the long-mark hypothesis above."

sibling_notes: The board hive:oai_math:review:fam:074 was empty when I checked, so no sibling input was available. The paper's main external dependency is the companion OpenAI preprint 'The Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions' (its Lemma 2.3). If a sibling branch audits that paper, its verdict matters directly here.
